text:
Weight-Space Programming showed a frontier model can read and write an LLM's weights.

Two follow-ups:
– can those edits be switched live, between tokens?
– who should decide when?

Then I rebuilt my edits WSP-style, from neuron values. More interesting than clean 🧵

2/ Qwen3.5-4B. Edits sit on down_proj outputs (bias patches, rank-1 projections, W_down column changes), gated by absolute token position.

Switching costs ~1µs, no measurable slowdown, and recall survives mid-conversation switches (24/24).

The mechanics aren't the bottleneck.

3/ Length-reducing edit, 96 sealed Qs × 2 seeds, blind-graded:

• Claude routes from question text: −20% words, core +0.5 pts [−2.1, 3.1]
• Qwen picks via tool call: −68% words, core −13.0 [−20.8, −5.2]
• Placebo tool call, no edit: −3.6 (n.s.)

4/ So the edit composes with the tool context: tuned in a bare chat, it's a different edit after "Mode 'lazy' is on."

Caveat: that was 8-bit MLX. On FP32 PyTorch (other hardware too), Qwen picked it on 11/48 arithmetic Qs (vs 35/48) and lost nothing. I haven't isolated why.

5/ Then the WSP-style redo:

• kernel over weights + saved reads
• 10 forward passes per task (activations, residuals, DLA)
• final edits restricted to W_down columns
• FP32 on 2×T4

Three tasks: LaTeX → plain math, ELI5 style, and fixing the self-selection failure.

6/ LaTeX. DLA localized it: L27 n1173 adds +2.2 logits to LaTeX openers (next: 0.73).

Silencing it: nothing.

The top 512 hold only 26% of positive attribution. Silencing them: −60% LaTeX density, numbers intact, but 20/20 held-out answers kept some. $$ rerouted to $.

7/ ELI5. Contrasting kid-style vs normal answers was a trap: it mostly measures the text. Matching every L16–31 neuron to its kid-text level closes only 27% of the gap.

A matched context (same text ± instruction) gave a clean signal:
+yummy +silly
−fundamentally

8/ But MLPs' direct writes cover only ~19% of that effect, and oppose it in L8–16. The rest comes via attention and indirect paths (untested causally).

Scaling can only amplify what's active. Best edit: 3,584 neurons ×4 → FK 10.7→7.2 on 20 held-out prompts, 1 loop. Prompt: 3.3.

9/ Self-selection. After the tool call, the edit gains a digit-promoting component, written entirely in L31 (flat through L30). Digit readout recovered from W31 by least squares.

But the fix built on it changed 2/11 steered answers. At FP32 there was little failure to fix.

10/ Takeaways for WSP-style loops:

• The kernel's best use was as a negative oracle: it ruled out approaches before I spent passes
• Contrast matched contexts, not texts
• For instruction-like behavior, W_down may be the wrong lever. Attention is next

11/ Live edits are cheap. The hard parts are deciding when to switch and building edits that beat a prompt.

Pre-registered. All 3 redo hypotheses failed as written. Paper, code, and the full controller trace (every read and edit Claude made):
